instruction: Change the heading font size to 16 in the document.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent selected the heading text correctly, then clicked 'Align Right' instead of 'Align Center', resulting in right-aligned heading instead of centered. Final screenshot shows cursor moved into table.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select text in Writer, interact with formatting toolbar buttons, navigate document
metadata.failure_analysis: Model confused the right-align button with center-align. It selected the correct text but applied the wrong formatting action.
metadata.task_rationale: Model demonstrated ability to select heading text and interact with the toolbar. Changing font size requires selecting text and modifying the font size field, which is a simpler single-value change within demonstrated capability.
metadata.explanation: Task asks to change heading font size to 16pt. Custom getter reads DOCX first paragraph runs and extracts font size. Metric compares with expected size (tolerance 0.5pt).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads DOCX first paragraph font size via python-docx, which is a reasonable proxy for the heading in a template document
Metric correctly accesses expected.get('expected_font_size') - proper handling for type='rule' where expected IS the rules dict
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring getter reads the latest state
0.5pt tolerance in metric comparison is appropriate for font size verification
Minor: getter only checks first run's font size (sizes[0]); if heading has multiple runs with different sizes, only the first is verified
Minor: getter uses run.font.size which returns directly-applied size only; if size is inherited purely from style, it may return None causing a false negative
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking all runs in the first paragraph to ensure all have the expected font size, not just the first run
Consider also checking the paragraph style's font size as a fallback when run.font.size is None (style-inherited sizes)
